name: JS Accessibility Fixer
author: JoomSky

sections.description:
JS Accessibility Fixer checks the pages of your site the way visitors get them, with your theme, page builder and plugins, and tells you in plain words what is wrong, why it matters, who can fix it and how.

It is not an overlay. It adds no toolbar for visitors and does not try to repair your site with a script. Problems are fixed where they come from: in the content, the theme or a plugin. The plugin shows you where that is.

What it does

  • Checks real pages. Each page is loaded in your browser, after scripts have finished, and checked with the open-source engine axe-core (WCAG 2.2 levels A and AA) plus eight rules of our own. The cart and checkout of a shop are checked with a test product in the cart; nothing is saved.
  • Says who fixes it. Every problem is marked as content (an editor fixes it in the page, a widget or the menu), theme, or plugin, with the name of the template part, widget area or plugin where possible, and a link to the place where it is fixed: the post (also in Elementor or Beaver Builder), the widgets, the menus, the site editor or the Customizer.
  • Explains every rule. Each of the 73 rules has a help page: why the problem matters, and steps for editors, for the theme and for plugins, with links to the WCAG success criteria.
  • Groups problems. A problem in the header appears once, with the number of pages, not a hundred times.
  • Keeps a dated record. “Ignore” and “Accept” decisions are stored with a reason, a name and a date, apply on every page, and stay after new checks. The decision log lists every decision, and every problem a new check no longer finds.
  • Works in the block editor. The “Accessibility” panel shows the problems of the page you edit and can check it after every update. “Show on page” outlines the problem element on the live page.
  • Guides the manual checks. 31 checks of what no machine can judge (keyboard use, screen reader, zoom, meaningful texts, captions, forms, touch, time limits), each with test steps and WCAG criteria. Every result is kept with the tester’s name and the date.
  • Drafts an accessibility statement from your results, for businesses (European Accessibility Act information) or for EU public sector bodies (model statement). The status is computed and can only be “fully compliant” when nothing is open, every manual check passed and every page was checked. Not legal advice.
  • Collects feedback from visitors with an accessible form (block or shortcode), without CAPTCHA. IP addresses are not stored; only a coded form of the address is kept for one hour, to limit misuse. Reports arrive in an inbox and by email, and work with the WordPress privacy tools.
  • Offers six safe automatic fixes, each with its own switch and off by default: a “Skip to content” link, a visible keyboard focus, no forced tab order, a note for links that open a new tab, the page language, and underlined links in text.

Our own screens are accessible

The plugin’s screens work with the keyboard alone: decisions are made in the row, without pop-up boxes, and focus stays where you are. Our own checker finds no problem on them.

What automated checks cannot do

Automated checks find only part of all accessibility problems. A clean result does not mean that a site meets WCAG or any law. That is why the plugin includes the manual checks, and why it never claims compliance on its own.

Privacy

  • No account, no sign-up, no external service. Check results stay in your database.
  • Nothing is loaded for visitors, except the feedback form where you place it and the safe fixes you switch on.
  • The help pages link to the W3C and to the makers of axe-core. These are plain links; nothing is sent until you click one.

Pro add-on

This plugin is complete on its own: nothing is locked or limited. The separate Pro add-on checks the whole site in one go, keeps the history of all scans with what is new and what was fixed, and lets you decide on many issues at once.

For developers

Add-ons can use these hooks:

  • jsaf_admin_tabs (filter) and jsaf_render_tab_{tab} (action): more tabs on the Accessibility screen
  • jsaf_admin_assets (action): scripts and styles on the Accessibility screen
  • jsaf_scan_screen (action): more options on the Scan screen
  • jsaf_overview_before_table (action): tools above the issue list
  • jsaf_scan_post_types (filter): the post types a site scan covers
  • jsaf_builder_block_namespaces (filter): block libraries whose blocks count as content
  • jsaf_shop_test_product_id (filter): the product put in the test cart
  • window.JSAFScanner: scanUrl, save, api, sleep, setBox (the page scanner)

The checking engine (engine/engine.js) contains no WordPress code. engine/rules.json lists every rule it runs, with its WCAG criteria.

External services

This plugin does not connect to any external service and sends no data anywhere. Checks run in your own browser, and results are stored in your WordPress database.

The help pages contain plain links to the WCAG documents of the W3C (www.w3.org) and to the rule descriptions of the makers of axe-core (dequeuniversity.com). Nothing is loaded from these sites; they open only when you click a link.

Third-party software

This plugin includes axe-core 4.14.1 by Deque Systems, Inc., unchanged, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (vendor/axe-core/LICENSE, source: https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core). See THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.

axe-core is a trademark of Deque Systems, Inc. in the US and other countries. This plugin is not made, endorsed or supported by Deque Systems, Inc.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin under Plugins > Add New, or upload the folder to wp-content/plugins.
  2. Activate it. A new menu item “Accessibility” appears.
  3. Open Accessibility > Scan and check your home page, or open any post in the block editor and use the “Accessibility” panel.
  4. Open Accessibility > Overview to see the problems, who fixes them and how.

Administrators and editors can run checks. Only administrators can change the settings.
sections.faq:
Does this make my site compliant with the law?

No plugin can do that. Automated checks find only part of all problems. This plugin finds what a machine can find, guides the checks a person must do, and keeps a dated record of both. Whether a site meets a law also depends on things outside the website.

Is this an overlay?

No. Overlays add a toolbar or a script that changes the page for visitors. This plugin finds problems so they can be fixed at their source. The six safe fixes change only small, well-understood things, and each one is off until you switch it on.

Does it slow down my site?

No. Checks run in your own browser when you start them. Nothing is loaded for visitors, except the feedback form where you place it and the safe fixes you switch on.

Does it send data anywhere?

No. There is no account and no external service. Results are stored in your WordPress database.

How does it know who must fix a problem?

During a check, WordPress marks the parts of the page with invisible comments: post content, widget areas, menus, template parts, blocks and shortcodes of plugins. The checker looks at the part around each problem. If no part can be found, it says “unknown”.

Which themes and page builders does it work with?

It checks the finished page, so it works with any theme and builder. “Who fixes it” was measured with Twenty Twenty-One, Twenty Twenty-Five and Astra, with Elementor, Spectra and Beaver Builder, and with WooCommerce.

What does “check by hand” mean?

Some problems need a person to decide. “Read more” can be clear in its context, and a heading level can be skipped on purpose. These are listed separately, are never counted as errors, and can be accepted with a reason.

Does it check the cart and checkout?

Yes. They are checked with one test product in the cart, so you see the real form. Nothing is saved: no cart, no session, no order.

What happens to my data when I delete the plugin?

By default the results, decisions, manual check results and feedback reports stay in the database, so the record is kept if you install the plugin again. To remove everything, switch on “Delete all accessibility data when the plugin is deleted” in Accessibility > Settings before you delete the plugin. Your pages, including the statement page, are never deleted.

Can I translate it?

Yes. All texts can be translated, including the help pages and the texts of the scripts. The template is languages/js-accessibility-fixer.pot.
